scenes.narration: Your incident response plan may exist. Your role matrix may exist. Your exercise records may exist. But that does not mean the evidence agrees.
scenes.title: The plan exists
scenes.visual: A response plan, contact register and exercise record sit apart.

scenes.narration: Plans, named owners, exercises and contact details age at different speeds. One stale record can hide inside an otherwise complete-looking folder.
scenes.title: Evidence ages differently
scenes.visual: Documents move across separate currency tracks.

scenes.narration: DIO Incident Readiness Proof maps what is supplied, what is missing, what is stale, and which decisions still require a named human authority.
scenes.title: Map before you rely
scenes.visual: The evidence resolves into coverage, currency and authority lanes.

scenes.narration: It does not certify readiness. It does not guarantee recovery. And it does not turn a generated dossier into operational authority.
scenes.title: No readiness theatre
scenes.visual: Unsupported certification and guaranteed recovery claims are visibly refused.

scenes.narration: The result is a reviewable, multi-format evidence dossier with a gap register, action boundary and hash-bound proof manifest.
scenes.title: A reviewable dossier
scenes.visual: A governed evidence register, gap register and proof manifest appear.

scenes.narration: Prepare a controlled review locally. Keep the consequential decision human. Know what your response plan can prove before the incident does.
scenes.title: Know before the incident does
scenes.visual: The local intake gate opens while external release remains locked.

title: Can Your Incident Plan Prove It?
